## Background

Today we are going to learn all about the  **ggplot2** package in R.

There are tons of graphics packages in R. These include "base R graphics" (like the `plot()` function we used last day) and add packages like **ggplot2**.

### Comparing base graphics with ggplot

We can use the in-build data frame `cars` to play with plotting:

```{r}
head(cars)
```

```{r}
plot(cars)
```
Now with ggplot:
First I need to install the package with `install.packages()` 

> I do not want to run `install.packages("ggplot")` in my quarto document as this will result in me re-installing the package every time I render my report.

Every time I want to use a function from a given package I need to load it up with a `library()` call:
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars)

```

Every ggplot needs at least 3 things:

- the **data**: (data.frame we want to plot from)
- the **aesthetics** (how the columns of the data map to the plot)
- the **geom** (how you want the plot drawn, points, lines, etc.)

```{r}
ggplot(data=cars) + 
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method="lm" ) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x= "Speed (MPH)", y="Stopping Distance (ft)", title="Silly Plot of Stopping Distances")
```



## Gene Expression Plot

Read the data from online:

```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
```

```{r}
ggplot(genes) + 
  aes(Condition1, Condition2) +
  geom_point()
```
> Q. How many genes are in this database?

```{r}
nrow(genes)
```
> Q. How many are "up" regulated?

```{r}
table(genes$State)
```

```{r}
sum(genes$State == "up")

```

>Q. What percentage of genes are "down" regulated?

```{r}
n.down <- sum(genes$State == "down")
n.total<- nrow(genes)

ans <- round(n.down/n.total * 100, 2)
ans
```

The percentage of down genes is `r ans` % and that is that ...

```{r}
myplot <- ggplot(genes) +
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2, col=State) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_colour_manual(values=c("blue", "pink", "purple"))+
  labs(title="Gene expression changes upon drug treatment ", x="Control (no drug)", y="Drug treated", subtitle= "GLP-1 inhibitor from Novo" ) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(10, 50, by = 10))
```

```{r}
myplot
```

We can install extra packages with `install.packages()` like theme packages for spongebob colors or actually useful ones like **patchwork** for combining plots:

```{r}
library(patchwork)

p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp))
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_boxplot(aes(gear, disp, group = gear))
p3 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_smooth(aes(disp, qsec))
p4 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_bar(aes(carb))

# Use patchwork to combine them here:
p1 / p2 | p3 / p4

```

```{r}
myplot + facet_wrap(~State)
```


## The GapMinder data

The gapminder dataset is rather famous and has lots of stuff we can plot ;) 

```{r}
# File location online
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"

gapminder <- read.delim(url)
```

Have a week peak:
```{r}
head(gapminder)
```

>Q. How many data entries are there in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(gapminder)
```
>Q. How many countries are in this dataset?

```{r}
length(unique(gapminder$country))
```

```{r}
ggplot(data=gapminder) +
  aes(gdpPercap, lifeExp, col=continent) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.5)
```

Break out a facet per con

```{r}
ggplot(data=gapminder) +
  aes(gdpPercap, lifeExp, col=continent) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~continent)
```


Hisograms
```{r}
ggplot(data=gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, color=continent, fill=continent) +
  geom_histogram()
```

and a boxplot 

```{r}
ggplot(data=gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, continent, fill=continent) +
  geom_boxplot()
```
geom_col(gapminder)
```{r}
geom_col(gapminder)
```
